zh.caseTitle: 病历：一场变了味的群聊争论
zh.testimony: 群里讨论该不该让孩子用平板学习。有人说平板伤眼睛，我回了一句「你连孩子都没养过，有什么资格谈教育？」然后有人说平板会让孩子沉迷游戏，我告诉他：照你这么说，反对用平板的人就是想让孩子彻底回到原始社会、连电视都不许看。后来又有人转了一篇「屏幕时间与近视」的研究链接，我还没来得及细看。再说了，我们小时候不也看电视长大吗？电视都没事，平板能有什么事？

textRefs.spot_hominem: 你连孩子都没养过，有什么资格谈教育
textRefs.spot_strawman2: 反对用平板的人就是想让孩子彻底回到原始社会、连电视都不许看
textRefs.spot_tradition: 我们小时候不也看电视长大吗？电视都没事，平板能有什么事
textRefs.debunk_hominem: 诉诸人身：用「没养过孩子」否定对方发言资格，而不是讨论「平板伤不伤眼睛」本身。
textRefs.debunk_strawman2: 稻草人：把「反对平板」曲解成「回到原始社会、不许看电视」的极端立场再攻击——反对者可能只是建议控制时长。
textRefs.debunk_tradition: 诉诸传统：「一直这么做」不等于「这么做是对的」——过去看没事，不代表平板与电视的风险完全一样。
textRefs.q_hominem: 有没有养过孩子，和他说的「平板伤眼睛」有没有道理是两回事吗？
textRefs.q_strawman2: 反对者的真实主张是「禁止一切屏幕」，还是只是「控制使用时间」？
textRefs.q_tradition: 电视和以前的我们没事，能证明平板对孩子也一定没事吗？
textRefs.q_d1: 说「沉迷游戏」的那位，他自己平时玩不玩游戏？
textRefs.q_d2: 过去没有平板时，学生的平均视力是不是更好？

hints: 攻击人，不攻击观点——这是人身攻击
把对方观点推到极端再打——这是稻草人
「我们以前也这样」——这是诉诸传统
zh.explanation: 这场争论里小张犯了三个谬误：①用「没养过孩子」堵嘴；②把「反对平板」歪曲成「回到原始社会」；③用「小时候看电视也没事」当理由。追问发言者自己玩不玩游戏仍是在看人不看论证；比较过去视力虽有参考价值，却混入年代、设备和生活方式差异，不能单独证明传统方案更好。

en.caseTitle: Record: A Group-Chat Argument Gone Wrong
en.testimony: The group was discussing whether kids should use tablets for learning. Someone said tablets hurt eyes, and I replied "you've never even raised a child, what right do you have to talk about education?" Then someone said tablets make kids addicted to games, and I told him: by that logic, people who oppose tablets want kids to go back to the Stone Age and ban TV entirely. Later someone shared a link to a study on "screen time and myopia", which I haven't had time to read closely. Anyway, didn't we all grow up watching TV? TV was fine, so how can tablets be a problem?

textRefs.spot_hominem: you've never even raised a child, what right do you have to talk about education
textRefs.spot_strawman2: people who oppose tablets want kids to go back to the Stone Age and ban TV entirely
textRefs.spot_tradition: didn't we all grow up watching TV? TV was fine, so how can tablets be a problem
textRefs.debunk_hominem: Ad hominem: denying someone's right to speak because they haven't raised a child, instead of discussing whether tablets actually hurt eyes.
textRefs.debunk_strawman2: Straw man: twisting "opposing tablets" into "returning to the Stone Age and banning TV" before attacking — opponents may just be suggesting limits on screen time.
textRefs.debunk_tradition: Appeal to tradition: "we've always done this" is not "this is right" — TV being fine in the past does not mean tablets carry identical risks.
textRefs.q_hominem: Does whether someone has raised a child change whether "tablets hurt eyes" makes sense?
textRefs.q_strawman2: Do opponents actually demand banning all screens, or just limiting usage time?
textRefs.q_tradition: Does TV being fine for us back then prove tablets are fine for kids now?
textRefs.q_d1: Does the person who mentioned game addiction play games himself?
textRefs.q_d2: Was students' average eyesight better in the years before tablets?

hints: Attacking the person instead of the point — that is ad hominem
Pushing an opponent's view to the extreme before attacking — that is a straw man
"We always did it this way" — that is an appeal to tradition
en.explanation: Xiao Zhang commits three fallacies: ① dismissing a speaker for not raising children; ② twisting caution about tablets into returning to the Stone Age; ③ treating childhood television as proof. Asking whether a critic plays games still judges the person. Comparing eyesight before tablets is relevant, but era, device, and lifestyle differences keep it from proving the traditional approach is better.
